statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r and r is the least integer X with 1 <= X such that cost(X) <= maxOperations, where cost(X) = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} (ceil_div(nums[i], X) - 1), and ceil_div(a, b) denotes the least integer q with q * b >= a (for positive integers a and b). Equivalently, 1 <= r, cost(r) <= maxOperations, and for every integer X with 1 <= X < r, cost(X) > maxOperations.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9 (maxOperations = 0 is allowed to cover the provided example [1000000000], 0 -> 1000000000).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; in particular, it does not panic, overflow, or fail due to out-of-bounds access. No further property of r is claimed by this specification.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 10^5; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9 (maxOperations = 0 is allowed to cover the provided example [1000000000], 0 -> 1000000000).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns r, then r >= ceil_div(max(nums), maxOperations + 1), where max(nums) = max_{0 <= i < len(nums)} nums[i] and ceil_div(a,b) denotes the least integer q with q * b >= a (b > 0).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns r, then r >= ceil_div(S, len(nums) + maxOperations), where S = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] and ceil_div(a,b) denotes the least integer q with q * b >= a (b > 0).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns r, then r <= ceil_div(max(nums), floor_div(maxOperations, len(nums)) + 1), where max(nums) = max_{0 <= i < len(nums)} nums[i], floor_div(a,b) is the greatest integer q with q * b <= a (a >= 0, b > 0), and ceil_div(a,b) is the least integer q with q * b >= a (b > 0).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, if the function returns r, then r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9; maxOperations >= S - len(nums), where S = sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i].

preconditions: len(nums) >= 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; 0 <= maxOperations <= 10^9; len(nums) = 1.
